Read core outlines from IGES files

Source: R/outline_iges.R
read_outline_iges.Rd

Reads the peripheral outline of each core from an IGES file and returns it as a closed loop of points, ready for fit_intersection_plane(), cpi_pra_batch() and plot_core().

Usage

read_outline_iges(files, ids = NULL, n_per_seg = 300, gap_frac = 0.01)

Arguments

files

Paths to IGES files (.igs / .iges), one per core.

ids

Core IDs, one per file, matching the ID column of the scar table. Default: the file names without extension.

n_per_seg

Number of points sampled along each B-spline segment. Default 300.

gap_frac

Largest gap between segment ends that is bridged with a straight chord, as a fraction of the outline's bounding-box diagonal. Default 0.01.

Value

A named list (names = ids) of numeric matrices with columns X, Y, Z, one point per row, ordered along the loop with the first point repeated as the last. Attributes record how the loop was assembled: n_segments, worst_gap (largest bridged gap), n_bridged, n_discarded (separate curves that were not part of the loop) and file. Files that cannot be read are left out with a warning.

Details

The outline must be exported as rational B-spline curves (IGES entity type 126), the form Geomagic Wrap and most CAD programs use for curves. Segments may come in any order and orientation; they are chained into connected loops. If an export carries stray curves away from the periphery, the longest closed loop is taken as the outline. Gaps between segment ends up to gap_frac of the outline's size are closed with a straight chord; larger gaps are an error, because a missing stretch of outline must not be invented. Files with other curve entities (arcs, polylines, offset curves) are rejected: export the outline as B-splines.

The declared IGES unit is ignored. The outline must be in the same coordinate frame as the scar coordinates of its core; cpi_pra_batch() checks this.

See also

fit_intersection_plane(), cpi_pra_batch(), plot_core()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
files    <- list.files("outlines", "\\.(igs|iges)$", full.names = TRUE)
outlines <- read_outline_iges(files)
names(outlines)

# File names that differ from the core IDs
outlines <- read_outline_iges(files, ids = c("EXP01", "EXP02"))
} # }
